name: pe_directories
description: Read the PE data directories that pe_info declares and does not read, through checked ranges (an RVA becomes a file offset only through a section that holds file bytes there; a table that runs off its section is a problem, never an empty list). Exports: every function with ordinal (base plus index), RVA, section, name (attached through the ordinal table) and forwarder string. Delay-load imports: libraries and function names or ordinals, in the RVA form and the old virtual-address form; each name table is read once (a table shared with, or starting inside, one already read is said and not listed again) and all of them together list at most 1,000,000 rows. TLS: the directory and the callback array, each callback with the section that holds it (a declaration: nothing says what a callback does). Resources: the type/name/language tree with each leaf's RVA, file offset and size; the version information (the fixed file version, file flags and a few well-known string keys by value, the others by name: claims the file makes about itself) and the manifest's requested execution level; extract resource:<row> writes a resource byte for byte. CLR header: runtime version, flags, entry point token, strong-name and managed-native fields as declarations, and the metadata root's version string and stream names and sizes (the metadata tables are read only with clr_tables: then the #~ stream's heap-size byte, valid mask, row counts and coded-index widths, and the rows of Module, TypeRef, TypeDef, Field, MethodDef, Param, MemberRef, ImplMap, Assembly, AssemblyRef and ManifestResource with their file offsets, names from #Strings, blobs by offset and size only, GUIDs from #GUID, and the #US user strings, every string through the sanitiser; a #- (uncompressed) or edit-and-continue stream, a heap-size byte with the delta bit, or a table above 0x2C is refused as unsupported, which makes the answer partial and names the reason; row counts of the other tables are given, their rows are not read; nothing is said about what a method does or about any signature). Debug directory: entry types and times (raw and UTC; with a REPRO entry no stamp is rendered as a time, they are build hashes) and the CodeView GUID, age and PDB path (a claim about the build machine). Rich header: raw decoded entries, not validated. A section whose PointerToRawData is not a multiple of FileAlignment (PE/COFF requires one of an executable image), and a FileAlignment outside 512..64K that is not equal to a SectionAlignment below the page size, are listed and are problems; the reading rule is stated beside them: with FileAlignment of 512 or more a value that is not a multiple of 512 is read from the value rounded down to 512, any other as written, and both values are given. Every bound (version blocks, strings, keys, stream headers, debug entries, descriptors) that is reached is a limit, and a version block whose length does not fit is a problem. No digest of an extracted resource is printed (with write_values, in a job, it goes to the values file). Every key and every value of the answer and of each file it names passes the sanitiser and then a backstop (the same shared block as doc_structure's; the backstop withholds any key or value the sanitiser would still change and makes the answer partial): a string out of the file is withheld by shape only, as doc_structure's manifest says (a secret of another shape is printed: read a file whose secrets matter in a job with secret_output; the whole only with write_values there), a string whose address points into the middle of a token run is sanitised whole and its head withheld, one longer than 2,048 characters is given by length only, two keys withheld to one text are both kept, a CodeView GUID whose bytes read as text (a run of nine token characters, or ten in all) is withheld, and no list in the answer is longer than the larger of limit and 100 items (a longer one is written whole to a file named beside it). A tool-output directory reached through a symbolic link is refused. Not read: import and base-relocation contents, exception tables, load configuration contents, resource contents beyond the version information and the manifest, CLR metadata tables (without clr_tables; with it, only the rows of the tables it lists) and method bodies, Authenticode (nothing is parsed or verified), and anything about what code does. Every answer carries status, problems, limits_hit and coverage; a budget that is reached is a limit. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer and the exit code 128 plus the signal from the moment the module has run as far as its stop handlers, which are installed at module level and not when main() starts (only the start of the interpreter and the compiling of the file come before); a second signal does nothing while the first is answered, and no hidden temporary file is left. SENSITIVE: write_values writes each value it withheld from the answer (a relationship target, a resource string, a name) whole to a file under $OUT, so the manifest declares secret_output for it and the tool checks SECRET_OUTPUT: in any run that is not a job run as secret output it is refused as JSON before anything is created. extract_to writes byte-for-byte parts of the document the examiner supplied into a directory the examiner names (mode 0600, created exclusively); it is not a value the tool found and is not a flag, so the declaration does not name it. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 7: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

extract_to.description: Where resources named in extract are written: a directory under work/<your agent id>/ (in a job, under $OUT). Files are created exclusively, mode 0600, named extract-NNNN.bin, and can contain secrets

extract.description: Resources to write byte for byte (at most 64): resource:<row number in the resources table>. Needs extract_to; run in a job with secret_output: true

write_values.description: Write each export forwarder, version string and PDB path whole to pe-directories-values.jsonl under $OUT, and the real name behind every withheld name (default false; refused outside a job; run the job with secret_output: true)

clr_tables.description: Also read the CLR metadata table stream (#~): heap sizes, valid mask, row counts and the rows of Module, TypeRef, TypeDef, Field, MethodDef, Param, MemberRef, ImplMap, Assembly, AssemblyRef and ManifestResource with file offsets, and the #GUID and #US heaps; a #- (uncompressed or edit-and-continue) stream is refused as unsupported (default false)

max_stream_bytes.description: Most bytes one resource may be read as (default 16777216)

max_total_bytes.description: Most bytes all extracted resources may total (default 134217728)

limit.description: Rows of one table kept in the answer (default 1000, at most 20000: a larger number is refused, as the rows are withheld while the file is read); the whole of a longer table is written to a file and named

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit for reading, in seconds, from 1 to 90 (default 70); a read that reaches it stops, reports what it read and says so. The rows of each table are withheld as they are read, under this limit; the rest of the answer is built after it and has until about 90 s after the call began, at least 5 s after the reading: a string it has no time to check is given by its length and the answer says so (partial). A call that has not answered within 105 s ends with a partial answer of the problems, the limits and the first rows of each table it holds, before the manifest's 120 s limit
